transcript:
Meeting header: 
Date: 2026-12-05 15:30 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Lina (Head of ML - Sable), Priya (ML Eng), Tom (Platform), Ethan (Procurement)

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, i'll kick us off. quick agenda — walkthrough of the Optimize console for precision profiles, show `INT8` vs `FP8` behavior on a few sample prompts, and then we want to land on a pilot scope. is that sound ok?

[00:22] Lina: yep that's great, thanks. our primary goals are latency under 120ms p95 for short queries and keeping any hallucination rates below our current baseline. we're also evaluating cost reduction — we have a rough target of 40% lower inference cost if possible.

[00:45] Maya: perfect. diego will show the console and then we'll talk rollout patterns. diego, over to you.

[00:51] Diego: cool, thanks. i'm opening the Optimize playbook — uh, excuse me,.. the Optimize tab in the Redwood Console. so first thing, we have "precision profiles"; you can see the curated INT8 and FP8 options. note: FP8 here is the mixed FP8 path we validated on the 70b family, int8 is lower-precision quant that often saves us 2-3x in memory and sometimes 20-40% per-token cost depending on batching.

[01:28] Priya: quick question—when you say 20-40% are you comparing hosted baseline or dedicated?

[01:35] Diego: good call. that's comparing hosted baseline with our standard FP16-ish runtime. for dedicated with advantages from batching and NVLink the delta moves, but still, INT8 typically reduces unit GPU time. sometimes the packaging of kernels means INT8 improves latency too because smaller memory copies, but there are cases where quantization overhead increases decode latency slightly, depends on kernel pairing.

[02:05] Tom: on the dedicated side we have constraints: we need to ensure the KV cache is isolated per-tenant and our networking must stay in our VPC. we'll probably lean to private deployment if we do a sustained pilot.

[02:21] Maya: that's fine — Redwood Private supports VPC + KMS integration; we'll include that in the runbook.

[02:30] Diego: demoing a live run — i'm pulling up three prompts that Priya uploaded earlier: a short search query, a multi-turn helpdesk-summarization and a clinical-style instruction. i'm going to run each at FP8, then INT8, and show per-token latency, PSNR-style quality score we computed from your eval set (note: the quality metric here is synthetic, actual quality should be validated on your prompts).

[03:05] [03:05] Diego: first prompt — a 12-token question. FP8 p95 78ms, mean 62ms, int8 p95 56ms, mean 43ms. cost estimate per 1k tokens reduces from $X to $Y — i'll attach the estimate.

[03:40] Priya: that latency improvement is appealing. can you show where the console exposes confidence in output fidelity? we need something that flags when INT8 diverges.

[03:52] Diego: yes — there's a fidelity dashboard. it shows delta responses vs baseline using our eval comparison and a token-level divergence score. we also have a policy engine: you can set automated fallback to FP8/FP16 for prompts that hit a divergence threshold or certain user classes.

[04:20] Lina: how often do you see false positives? I mean, will the policy bounce calls too much and hurt latency?

[04:29] Diego: good question. typical false positives are low if you tune thresholds on a representative sample. we recommend an initial canary at 5% traffic with a 48–72 hour window, then expand to 25% with monitoring. our consoles show expected rollback rates based on prior customers — usually under 2% carry-forward.

[04:50] Ethan: from procurement perspective we need clear SLAs. if we route 95% traffic to INT8 and latency spikes, what's the remediation footprint?

[05:00] Maya: remediation options: automatic fallback, traffic steering to a different model family, and Dedicated burst capacity. we'll include a proposed SLA appendix for the pilot.

[05:12] Diego: showing a case study — small ecommerce platform saw 35% cost reduction with INT8 while maintaining classification accuracy, they used per-route policies and conservative thresholds for financial flows. not the same domain as Sable but similar pattern.

[05:40] Priya: any known prompt patterns that break INT8? our sensitive prompts include long clinical narratives and precise numeric extraction.

[05:50] Diego: long numeric-heavy sequences can have degraded calibration under extreme quant. FP8 tends to preserve numerical fidelity better. we typically mark extraction/financial/medical paths to be excluded from INT8 until they've passed a sensitivity sweep.

[06:10] Lina: ok. can you talk about monitoring — what telemetry do you expose? we need token-level latency, per-route error rate, output-delta histogram, and raw outputs for audit.

[06:22] Maya: console exposes token-level histograms, per-model traces, and we provide webhook hooks to ship full outputs to your SIEM or storage with redaction filters. audit logs, SSO via SAML, and KMS integrations are available for Private.

[06:45] Tom: how does KV cache behave across precision changes? if we fall back mid-stream does the KV cache mismatch cause artifacts?

[06:55] Diego: the runtime maintains model-variant-aware KV handling. if you switch from INT8 to FP8 mid-session, we can replay a compatible prefix or we fall back with a short reconnect — there may be a small latency bump but we avoid corruption. sometimes transcripts call this out as "K V cash" in older transcribes — the point being we manage cache coherency.

[07:25] Priya: can we do an A/B style comparison in production without duplicating cost?

[07:33] Diego: yes — we support shadowing and sampled A/B, where we run a fraction of calls in parallel as non-billable comparisons, storing the alternative outputs for evaluation. that lets you run fidelity checks with low incremental cost while mainline remains on FP8/INT8.

[07:55] Maya: i'm going to pull up the pilot runbook. the proposed scope: 2-week benchmark lab (us-run on Redwood infra), then a 4-week pilot in your staging (private deployment) with 5% canary expanding to 25% if thresholds pass. success criteria: p95 latency < 120ms, quality delta < 2% on your labeled set, and unit cost reduction >= 30%.

[08:30] Lina: that aligns. timeline — we aim to have pilot in January, but we'd like the lab results this month so we can plan budget.

[08:42] Maya: we can fast-follow the lab this week if you share prompts and traffic sample. we sent a benchmark template moments ago — i'll re-share.

[08:52] [08:52] Maya: note: the benchmark template lives here: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-link-sable-optimize and the deck is https://redwood.app/deck/optimize-qprofiles (we'll send the short recording too).

[09:10] Diego: showing the console's quality playback — here's an example where INT8 truncated a numeric list incorrectly on the clinical prompt; the console flagged it with a high divergence score and auto-triggered fallback in the canary run.

[09:35] Priya: we need visibility into the raw outputs (even redacted) to do human eval. is that possible with Private?

[09:42] Maya: yes; with Private you control retention and logs. we can set the pipeline to ship outputs to your S3 or GCS with encryption KMS.

[10:00] Ethan: curious about pricing model during pilot — is it still per-token or some blended reserved rate?

[10:08] Maya: for pilots we typically do usage billing with an optional short-term reserved node for predictable throughput. If you commit to a 3-month pilot we can provide a blended pilot rate; we'll include an estimate in the pricing doc.

[10:22] Tom: are there known vendor lock-in concerns with FP8/INT8 kernels — e.g., if we want to move between clouds or in-house later?

[10:32] Diego: we aim to use portable quantization formats and provide model artifacts and quantization recipes. some bits of kernel optimizations are hardware specific, but our orchestration layer abstracts routing so you can move between vendors with a migration plan. we'll provide the quant recipes and test artifacts.

[11:00] Lina: let's talk about risk acceptance. acceptable rollback rate and who signs off?

[11:08] Maya: we recommend product + ML + platform leads sign off on canary expansion. rollback threshold example: if divergence > 2% on labeled critical prompts OR p95 latency > 180ms for a sustained 30-minute window we auto-rollback. sign-off templates are in the runbook.

[11:35] Diego: showing the console's auto-alerts — you can pipe these to pagerduty or Slack and set escalation policies.

[11:50] Priya: one more technical — does INT8 impact sampling diversity (nucleus/top-p) behaviors? we've seen low-temp sampling drift with some quant strategies.

[12:02] Diego: yes, low-temp sampling can get a bit more peaky; we recommend re-evaluating sampling hyperparams during sensitivity sweeps. the Optimize console lets you run batch sweeps across temperature/top-p and produce a quality-vs-latency matrix.

[12:30] Maya: quick recap — deliverables from Redwood: benchmark lab results, pilot pricing estimate, and a suggested canary policy (Maya/Diego). from Sable: sample prompts, traffic sample, and sign-off on SLAs (Lina/Priya/Tom). we'll aim to have the lab results by Dec 9.

[12:55] Lina: sounds good. any blockers from your side for us to share prompts? data residency concerns — some prompts include PII in records.

[13:05] Maya: for the lab you can sanitize or we can sign an NDA + use Private infra. either works; for speed sanitize a sample first.

[13:18] Ethan: procurement note — we'll need an appendix for liability around hallucinations for the pilot scope. can you provide standard language?

[13:26] Maya: yes we'll include a standard pilot appendix and legal contacts.

[13:35] Priya: final technical ask — can Diego provide a short checklist for safe INT8 rollout?

[13:41] Diego: absolutely. checklist will include: 1) sensitivity sweep on labeled prompts, 2) set conservative divergence thresholds, 3) start 5% canary, 4) enable auto-fallback and logging, 5) review outputs for 72 hours, 6) expand traffic in staged increments. i'll put that in the action items.

[14:05] Maya: great — any other Qs?

[14:08] Lina: none here. thanks, this was productive.

[14:12] Maya: thanks everyone — we will send the materials and follow up with dates.

[14:18] Diego: thanks all.

End of transcript.

Notes about transcription quality: occasional mis-attributions and small filler words omitted; some product names were transcribed inconsistently (e.g., "Optimize" -> "Optomize" in a few spots). We preserved conversational interruptions and timing.
